newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Prince Andrew tours HK army base and airport site.
newsitem.headline: Prince Andrew tours HK army base and airport site.

text.p: Britain's Prince Andrew toured military and infrastructure sites in Hong Kong on Wednesday during one of the last royal visits before the colony reverts to Chinese rule in the middle of next year.

The Duke of York flew, dressed in combat fatigues, flew into the army base on Stonecutters Island, in the middle of Hong Kong harbour, where the 1st Battalion of the Staffordshire regiment, of which he is Colonel-In-Chief, is stationed.
He also toured the huge Tsing Ma suspension bridge linking Lantau island and the mainland of Hong Kong with an expressway and railway corridor to the new Chek Lap Kok airport.
Andrew's visit is one of the last by a member of the royal family before this freewheeling capitalist territory of 6.3 million people reverts to China next July 1.
Queen Elizabeth's second son received a cool reception from local media. Only eight journalists turned up to cover his visit to Stonecutters Island.
The British garrison is gradually scaling down ahead of Hong Kong's return to China.
Britain's armed forces in the colony, now numbering almost 3,000, will be cut to 1,500 six weeks before the date.
From July 1, China's People's Liberation Army will form the garrison with up to 10,000 troops, matching the British at their former peak troop strength.
